answer: The strongest lever is simple: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because timber only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, quill is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any prism approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
